key_insight: Organic photovoltaic performance hinges on CT–CS energy alignment balancing charge generation against voltage loss, with triplet recycling determining whether that balance survives at device level.
engineering_relevance: The proposed design window combines LE–CT offsets of 0.15–0.20 eV, weakly exothermic CT–CS offsets of 0.05–0.075 eV, and CT–T offsets no greater than about 0.1 eV for effective triplet recycling.
method: Couple exciton kinetics to device-level drift–diffusion transport.
Solve state populations and reversible photophysical transitions self-consistently.
Evaluate energy offsets and triplet-transfer kinetics under transient and steady-state conditions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the model reproduces triplet-mediated recombination in PM6:Y6 and material-dependent triplet recycling in D18:NFA blends.
watch_item: The abstract provides no quantitative validation errors or broad experimental testing of the proposed design windows; this is a physics-based model, not an AI method.
paper_title: Device Model Linking Singlet and Triplet Spin-State Properties to Organic Photovoltaic Device Characteristics
